name: Ozark Forest and Streams
blurb: Acorns, glades and spring-fed rivers: from deer and bears to hellbenders.

tip.title: Fail the acorn crop
tip.text: Acorns feed deer, turkeys, squirrels and bears. Set Oaks to -60% and watch the forest animals, then the bobcats and coyotes that hunt them.

nodes.desc: Eats leaves, twigs, fruits and nuts of trees and shrubs and the foliage of herbs, per the MDC. Coyotes and bobcats prey on it.
A nut-eater that harvests acorns and hickory nuts in the oak-hickory forest and is prey for bobcats and coyotes.
Chew glade grasses and wildflowers. The MDC lists grasshoppers as food for collared lizards, and turkeys eat insects too.

nodes.name: Aquatic insects
nodes.desc: Larvae graze algae in clear streams. Adults hatch into the air, where gray bats and fish catch them.
Stalks rabbits, squirrels, turkeys and deer fawns. The MDC names bobcats as deer predators.

nodes.name: Eastern collared lizard
nodes.desc: Lives on sunny, rocky glades and eats grasshoppers, beetles, spiders and even small lizards and snakes. Snakes and hawks prey on it.
Roosts in caves and hunts night-flying insects, many with aquatic larvae, over streams and reservoirs. Depends on a few cold winter caves and warmer summer caves.

nodes.name: American black bear
nodes.desc: Omnivore that fattens on acorns in late fall and also eats plants, insects, fawns and carrion. Once nearly eliminated from Missouri but now growing.
A flexible predator. The MDC names coyotes among animals that kill deer, and it also takes turkeys and squirrels.

nodes.name: Northern river otter
nodes.desc: Fish are the main food and crayfish a close second, per Wikipedia. Hunts the streams and rivers.
Powers the forest canopy, glade plants and stream algae.
Feeds the forest and, by soaking into limestone, the springs and streams.
The NPS says fire management helps collared lizards and turkeys by keeping glades and woodlands open.
Limestone and chert soils hold the oak-hickory forest; glade soils are especially thin.

nodes.name: Fungi, insects & bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down leaf litter and dead animals and return nutrients to the soil.
